name: Massachusetts
basePeriod: The last four completed calendar quarters before your claim. Massachusetts can use the last three plus your weeks in the current quarter if those do not qualify.

dependentAllowances.note: $25 a week for each child you mainly support, paid on top of the weekly rate.

notModeled: DUA states 30 weeks today; the law lowers it to 26 when unemployment is low statewide, as it did for claims from July 2023.
Benefit years that began before October 4, 2026 use a $1,105 maximum.

citation.sourceDocument: DUA, How unemployment insurance benefits are determined (2026); M.G.L. c. 151A §§1, 24, 29, 30
citation.sourceNote: DUA: "As of October 4, 2026, the maximum weekly benefit amount is $1,154.00 per week"; up to "30 times your weekly benefit amount, or 36% of your total wages in your base period"; "the maximum duration of benefits is 30 weeks"; and "a dependency allowance of up to $25 per child." c. 151A §1(w): the average weekly wage is the two highest quarters over 26, or the highest over 13 with wages in two quarters or fewer, raised to the next dollar; §29(a): the rate is "fifty percent" of it, rounded down; §30 adds dependency benefits on top of the cap. §24: base-period wages of at least $6,300 for 2026 and 30 times the rate. One unpaid waiting week. Read 2026-10-19.
